text:
Ivy: hi team, first week here — trying to reconcile dotfiles that use nix flakes with our asdf-based quickstart on my M2. brew stuff and rosetta-installed binaries are confusing my PATH and gpg/ssh agents are fighting. any pointers?
Rohan: welcome Ivy! :wave: few quick Qs: do you want to use nix as the primary package manager or stick with Homebrew + asdf? mixing both is doable but you need to decide which owns the core runtimes.
Ivy: i'd prefer nix flakes for reproducible envs but our repo scripts assume `asdf install --all`. i tried to run the flakes devshell and then `asdf` inside it fails: command not found.
Keira: flakes open a clean shell; they don't inherit your user PATH by default. If you expect asdf in the devshell, either add asdf to the flake devInputs or have the devshell source your profile. Example in flake.nix devShells.default.preBuild: add `home-manager` or `pkgs.asdf` so asdf is available.
Ivy: ah ok. i added `asdf` as a dependency in the flake; now asdf command exists but plugins can't install because gpg missing in the flake environment.
Rohan: include `gnupg` in devInputs or install gpg via nix. Alternatively, run plugin install outside the flake in your user env and check `.tool-versions` into repo.
Ivy: did that. separate weirdness: i have both arm brew under /opt/homebrew and an older intel brew under /usr/local from a previous machine. GUI apps launched from Finder pick up the intel /usr/local first and VS Code terminal shows node v20 while my asdf installed node is v18.
Keira: GUI apps use login shell envs; put PATH edits in `~/.zprofile` to ensure they inherit it. Prepend `/opt/homebrew/bin` at the top: `export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"`. Also uninstall the stale intel brew if possible: `rm -rf /usr/local/Homebrew` after confirming no dependencies.
Ivy: tried that, but Rosetta 2 still has some intel binaries (like some vendor CLI) that only run under x86. I need both archs available. any safe pattern?
Rohan: keep /opt/homebrew as primary. For the handful of intel-only tools, use `arch -x86_64 /usr/local/bin/some-cli` or install intel brew into a different prefix and call them explicitly. Avoid mixing bin directories in PATH order.
Ivy: got it. last big headache: gpg/ssh confusion. I have GPG signing and 1Password ssh agent enabled. gpg-agent sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK and overrides 1Password socket sometimes, then git push prompts for passphrase.
Keira: decide on one agent. If you want 1Password as primary, disable gpg-agent's ssh support: in `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` add `enable-ssh-support` only if you want gpg to act as agent — otherwise comment it out and restart `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent`. Make sure `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` exported points to 1Password socket before any other agent starts.
Ivy: I tracked a `.envrc` that does `eval "$(gpg-agent --daemon)"` in a repo — that was spawning a new agent and stomping the socket. removed it and now `ssh-add -l` shows keys from 1Password. GPG signing still uses my private key via gpg though.
Rohan: for git signing, use GPG_TTY export and ensure `gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format LONG` shows key. If you want both: let gpg own signing and 1Password handle SSH, but avoid letting either auto-spawn in project hooks.
Ivy: awesome. one more tiny VS Code tip: when using the nix devcontainer extension, the container won't see my host asdf unless i add `postCreateCommand` to run `asdf plugin-add --no-install nodejs` etc. so i added a small bootstrap script in devcontainer.json and it works.
Keira: nice. we should add a note in the onboarding doc about nix flakes + asdf edge cases.
Ivy: thanks all, everything is much smoother now — nix devshells provide reproducibility, asdf still manages per-project runtimes, PATH cleaned, and ssh/gpg agents no longer conflict. :tada:
DevEx Bot: Congrats Ivy! Helpful resources: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup, https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles, and please open a short PR to the onboarding docs about nix+asdf tips so future hires benefit.
